speaker: Dr Lily Neo
text: asked	the Minister for Health now that the World Health Organization has declared Zika as an international public health emergency (a) what are the additional measures implemented to better protect Singaporeans against Zika; and (b) whether there are inter-Ministry collaborations to prevent and control the spread of Zika here.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked	the Minister for Health whether the Ministry will consider (a) testing blood samples from travellers coming in from areas with ongoing Zika outbreaks and (b) requiring blood donors who have travelled to affected countries to wait at least 28 days before allowing them to donate blood, as advised by the World Health Organization and implemented in Hong Kong, Canada and Britain.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: WHO further noted that there was strong association of the PHEIC with Zika virus transmission in the affected areas.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The National Environment Agency (NEA) has an ongoing surveillance programme for Zika virus since 2014.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Prior to the WHO's declaration, the Ministry of Health (MOH) and NEA had already enhanced the surveillance, as well as stepped up measures, to reduce the risk of the Zika virus taking root in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: All doctors have been advised to stay vigilant against possible cases of Zika virus infection and on the protocols for testing and managing of suspect and confirmed cases.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So far, there has not been any reported case of Zika virus infection in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To reduce the risk of Zika becoming entrenched in Singapore, all confirmed cases will be admitted to Tan Tock Seng Hospital until they recover and test negative for the virus.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: MOH will also screen people in the vicinity of the home and workplace of confirmed cases for Zika virus infection.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, we have issued advisories to travellers to and from Zika-affected countries on how to protect themselves against mosquito bites.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have also reminded travellers who have returned to Singapore from affected areas to monitor their health and consult a doctor if they have symptoms of Zika, such as fever, skin rashes, joint and muscle pains, headaches and red eyes, and to reveal their travel history to their doctor.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If they have such symptoms after coming back from areas with Zika transmission, blood samples will be taken for Zika testing.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In the light of WHO's declaration, MOH and NEA have worked together to introduce additional measures.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: MOH is expanding Zika virus testing capability to more public hospital laboratories.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA has also stepped up the testing of blood samples from patients with fever and rash and suspected dengue for Zika as part of its Zika virus surveillance efforts.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Given the suspected link between Zika virus infection during pregnancy and microcephaly in newborns, MOH has also set up a Clinical Advisory Group on Zika virus infection and pregnancy to provide expert advice on the management of pregnant women with Zika virus infection.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: MOH is also looking at potential areas for collaboration and research with the relevant institutions on Zika virus diagnostics, transmission and the association with microcephaly and GBS.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, if a case is detected here, NEA and other agencies under the Inter-Agency Dengue Task Force, such as the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and the Public Utilities Board (PUB), will intensify search and destroy efforts to control the Aedes mosquito population at the implicated sites to contain any potential spread.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Page: 27 As Zika is transmitted through the same Aedes mosquito that transmits dengue, vector control remains the mainstay to prevent transmission of the Zika virus.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA has stepped up its vector control efforts, in partnership with the community, agencies and stakeholders, to control the mosquito population.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA has also brought forward the annual "Do the Mozzie Wipeout" campaign this year − in fact, it was held yesterday − as part of its community outreach efforts to raise awareness of the "5-Step Mozzie Wipeout" and urge the community to take immediate action to prevent mosquito breeding.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: All of us can do our part by taking the appropriate precautions to prevent mosquito breeding.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: What sort of directive will MOH give to practising doctors looking after Zika-affected pregnant patients with microcephaly foetuses with regard to termination of pregnancy?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Lastly, should circumstances arise, would MOH provide multiple free ultrasound screening follow-up for Zika-affected pregnant patients to ascertain microcephaly?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The clinical advisory group has just met and is still discussing their recommendations on the clinical management of pregnant women with confirmed or suspected Zika virus infection.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Notwithstanding this, it is noted that in Singapore, in fact, all pregnant women are already recommended to undergo routine ultrasound scans as part of antenatal check-ups.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Any abnormal foetal development, including microcephaly, that is picked up during these scans will be followed up by their doctors.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The doctor is in the best place to provide advice to the individual cases.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Termination of pregnancy is a personal choice made by the parents in consultation with their doctor.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, if patients have any financial difficulties, they will be referred to the medical social worker proactively and financial assistance will be given after means testing.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: MediFund also covers obstetrics care to ensure good antenatal care for all pregnancies and to optimise pregnancy outcomes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will consider this and other issues after the clinical advisory group has made its recommendations.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In the event of a Zika virus outbreak, are there lessons from the severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS) virus outbreak that MOH could apply?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: SARS and Zika viruses are spread through different modes of transmission.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: SARS is spread from person to person, while Zika is spread by mosquitoes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Containment measures like isolation of cases, contact tracing and quarantine of close contacts are important for SARS.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Measures to admit a confirmed case, isolate him until he recovers and the history of the virus will not work anymore.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, we will move to containment and mitigation measures and this means that we will take measures similar to dengue prevention and control – that is, source reduction.
